scope.summary: This standard defines terms, classifications, and nomenclature relating to various types of power-driven road vehicles (including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and quadricycles) and their trailers, establishing a standardized baseline for whole-vehicle type approval, registration, and Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) compliance across India.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural and Classification Specification (Automotive Homologation / Vehicle Testing)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Code. Under Rule 2 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all motor vehicles and trailers manufactured or registered in India must be classified and type-approved in accordance with the vehicle categories defined in IS 14272:2011 (which officially replaced the legacy industry code AIS-053:2005). Successful compliance is certified by authorized testing agencies (such as ARAI, GARC, and ICAT) via a Type Approval Certificate. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Applies an additional 'G' suffix designation to M or N vehicles that satisfy strict geometric off-road requirements (such as minimum approach, departure, and ramp breakover angles, ground clearances under axles, and all-wheel drive capabilities) per IS 12218.

Specifies definitions for the type of bodywork for passenger cars of Category M1 (comprising Saloon, Hatchback, Station Wagon, Coupe, Convertible, and Multi-purpose vehicles) to standardize registration.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14272 : 2011 (Reaffirmed 2025) is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing the official classification system, terminology, and nomenclature for all road-going motor vehicles and trailers in India. Developed by the Sectional Committee on Automotive Body and Chassis (TED 06) and officially incorporated into Rule 2 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, this first revision consolidated and replaced the previous standard IS 14272 (Part 1) and the industry standard AIS-053. It defines the technical boundaries for four-wheeled passenger transport (M1, M2, M3), goods transport (N1, N2, N3), less-than-four-wheelers/quadricycles (L1 to L7), and towed trailers/semi-trailers (T1 to T5), ensuring a standardized, legally binding framework for whole-vehicle type approval, registration, and emissions compliance.
